Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, the **exact solutions** to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+{30}^{∘})=\sqrt{3},$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$  are

worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}x+{30}^{∘} & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={60}^{∘}-{30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={30}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={30}^{∘}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={210}^{∘}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ 

So, in ascending order,  the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1}={30}^{∘},\,{x}_{2}={210}^{∘}.
$$
